title: Database Indexes And Search Flashcard Feed
summary: Passive database index and PostgreSQL search cards for short mobile review sessions.
audience: Backend, full-stack, and platform engineers reviewing database indexing and search behavior.

cards.title: Indexes Are Read Models
cards.prompt: A database index is a maintained read structure, not a free lookup spell.
cards.explanation: Every index trades faster matching query shapes for write overhead, storage, vacuum work, and migration cost. Review the workload that pays for it.

cards.title: Leftmost Prefix
cards.prompt: Composite B-tree indexes are strongest when queries constrain leading columns in order.
cards.explanation: An index on account_id and created_at is designed around account first. A query that only filters created_at may not benefit much.

cards.title: GIN Is Inverted
cards.prompt: GIN stores component keys such as lexemes, trigrams, or array elements.
cards.explanation: Instead of one scalar key per row, GIN maps extracted components to candidate rows. That makes it fit containment and text search shapes.

cards.title: Document Meets Query
cards.prompt: PostgreSQL full text search matches tsquery against tsvector with @@.
cards.explanation: The document and query are both parsed into normalized search structures before matching; this is not raw substring search.

cards.title: Rank Is Local
cards.prompt: ts_rank and ts_rank_cd are ordering signals inside one query, not universal relevance percentages.
cards.explanation: Normalization can scale scores, but it does not make ranks comparable across unrelated queries or a durable product quality metric.

cards.title: Trigrams Handle Typos
cards.prompt: pg_trgm compares overlapping three-character fragments to find similar strings.
cards.explanation: A misspelling can still share enough trigrams with the intended word for useful candidate generation.

cards.title: Threshold Is Tuning
cards.prompt: pg_trgm.similarity_threshold decides which fuzzy candidates the % operator admits.
cards.explanation: Lower thresholds help typo-heavy short searches but increase candidate volume and irrelevant matches. Tune with real search examples.

cards.title: Hybrid Candidate Sets
cards.prompt: Hybrid search often combines precise FTS candidates with fuzzy trigram candidates.
cards.explanation: FTS catches exact lexeme matches. Trigrams catch typos. The ranking layer decides how those signals compete.

cards.title: Index Review
cards.prompt: Before adding an index, name the exact query shape it supports.
cards.explanation: If the index cannot be tied to a real predicate, sort, and result size, it is likely to become maintenance cost without clear benefit.

cards.title: Partial Index Fit
cards.prompt: Use partial indexes for stable hot subsets, not as a substitute for partitioning.
cards.explanation: The query predicate must imply the index predicate. Many overlapping partial indexes can make planning and maintenance worse.

cards.title: Expression Must Match
cards.prompt: An expression index on lower(name) expects queries to use lower(name).
cards.explanation: Changing the query to raw name or unaccent(lower(name)) changes the indexed expression and may prevent index usage.

cards.title: Choose Search Config
cards.prompt: Use simple or english text search configuration intentionally.
cards.explanation: English stemming helps prose. Simple configuration can be better for titles, names, tags, codes, and labels where literal matching matters.

cards.title: Store The Vector
cards.prompt: Frequently searched documents usually deserve a stored tsvector or generated column.
cards.explanation: Recomputing to_tsvector in every query can be wasteful. Stored vectors make the query and matching GIN index easier to reason about.

cards.title: Use SET LOCAL
cards.prompt: Use SET LOCAL for request-specific trigram thresholds on pooled connections.
cards.explanation: A plain SET can leak a relaxed threshold into later requests on the same connection. SET LOCAL clears when the transaction ends.

cards.title: Extensions Are Setup
cards.prompt: CREATE EXTENSION belongs in migrations or database setup, not every search query.
cards.explanation: Extensions create database objects. Search requests should assume the schema exists and only tune request-local settings when needed.

cards.title: Tie-Break Search Results
cards.prompt: Add a deterministic tie-breaker after rank, such as id.
cards.explanation: Stable ordering matters for repeatable tests and pagination. Rank alone can leave equal-score rows in unstable order.

cards.title: Compound B-Tree Snippet
cards.prompt: Read the index order as account first, recent orders second.
cards.explanation: The query must use account_id for this index to be highly selective before created_at ordering matters.
cards.code:
create index orders_account_created_idx
  on orders (account_id, created_at desc);

cards.title: Partial Index Snippet
cards.prompt: Read the predicate as part of the index contract.
cards.explanation: Only unfulfilled orders are indexed. Queries must include or imply fulfilled_at is null to use this index.

cards.title: Weighted Vector Snippet
cards.prompt: Read title as A weight and body as C weight.
cards.explanation: setweight lets title matches outrank body-only matches when ranking consults the weighted vector.

cards.title: FTS GIN Snippet
cards.prompt: Read this as a GIN index over a stored search document.
cards.explanation: The search query should use the same search_document column with @@ so the index can filter candidates.

cards.title: Drizzle Trigram Snippet
cards.prompt: Read this as a GIN trigram expression index over lower(name).
cards.explanation: gin_trgm_ops tells PostgreSQL to extract trigram keys from the lower(name) expression for fuzzy matching.

cards.title: Trigram Query Snippet
cards.prompt: Read % as candidate admission and similarity as ranking.
cards.explanation: The WHERE clause can use the trigram index, while ORDER BY ranks the filtered candidate set.
cards.code:
where lower(title) % lower($1)
order by similarity(lower(title), lower($1)) desc

cards.title: Hybrid Candidates Snippet
cards.prompt: Read UNION ALL as keeping both FTS and trigram evidence.
cards.explanation: Rows can come from both passes. A later grouped score can keep the best signal or add a combined-match bonus.
cards.code:
select id, fts_rank as rank from fts_candidates
union all
select id, trigram_rank as rank from trigram_candidates

cards.title: SET LOCAL Snippet
cards.prompt: Read this as request-scoped threshold tuning.
cards.explanation: The threshold applies within the transaction and clears when the transaction ends.

cards.title: Index Cost Interview
cards.prompt: A teammate says every frequently filtered column should get an index. How do you respond?
cards.explanation: A strong answer discusses exact query shape, selectivity, returned rows, write amplification, storage, migration risk, and plan verification.

cards.title: Partial Index Interview
cards.prompt: When would you use a partial index instead of a normal index?
cards.explanation: Use it when a stable predicate selects a small hot subset and the target queries include or imply that predicate.

cards.title: FTS Versus LIKE Interview
cards.prompt: Why is full text search different from lower(body) like '%term%'?
cards.explanation: FTS parses documents into lexemes and queries into tsquery values. LIKE is character pattern matching and has different index behavior.

cards.title: Rank Caveat Interview
cards.prompt: Why should a product not display ts_rank_cd as a percent match?
cards.explanation: The score is a query-local ranking signal and does not use global corpus statistics. It is useful for ordering, not universal quality.

cards.title: Trigram Index Interview
cards.prompt: Explain what lower(name) gin_trgm_ops means in a PostgreSQL index.
cards.explanation: It is a trigram operator-class index over the lower(name) expression. Compatible queries must use the same normalized expression.

cards.title: Threshold Tuning Interview
cards.prompt: What can go wrong when pg_trgm.similarity_threshold is lowered too far?
cards.explanation: More weak matches enter the candidate set, increasing ranking work, latency, and irrelevant results unless other filters and ranking signals control it.

cards.title: Hybrid Ranking Interview
cards.prompt: Why might a hybrid query multiply trigram similarity by 0.8?
cards.explanation: It is a business weighting choice that lets exact FTS matches usually outrank fuzzy typo matches with similar raw scores.

cards.title: Extension Placement Interview
cards.prompt: Why should CREATE EXTENSION not live in a normal search query?
cards.explanation: Extensions are schema setup. Runtime search should rely on migrated database capabilities and keep request-specific settings transaction-local.
